name: Moscovium

discovery.discoverer: Joint Russian-American team, Dubna & Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced only via particle accelerator fusion, atom by atom.
majorUses: No practical applications — pure superheavy-element research
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive; observed only as individual atoms with sub-second half-lives.
notableCharacteristics: Named after Moscow Oblast, the region in Russia home to the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research at Dubna, in recognition of the lab's role in synthesizing many superheavy elements.
whyHere: Predicted to sit in Group 15 below bismuth, moscovium is expected to show a similarly variable +1/+3 oxidation chemistry, continuing the trend of relativistic effects increasingly stabilizing lower oxidation states toward the bottom of heavy p-block groups.
didYouKnow: Moscovium was created as part of the same joint Russian-American research collaboration at Dubna that also produced flerovium, livermorium, and tennessine — a rare case of Cold-War-rival nations co-discovering four elements together.
genZNote: Made by a joint Russia-US science team, which is honestly kind of wholesome given the history. Four elements' worth of actual cooperation.
